_doc: Per-map arrival narration (StoryHooks, at run start). Pool map_arrival.<map id> (data/maps/*.json ids); if nothing is eligible the generic run_start pool plays instead. Story var map_runs.<id> counts runs on each map (already incremented when these play).

lines.text: The Ruined Sanctum. Here the fallen first broke through, and here the chapels still lie where they toppled. No walls. No end. Only more of them.
Burnt graveyards and broken bells. The Sanctum remembers you, {demon}. It still smells of the last time.
The border of the mortal realm. Every step you take here, the Verge forgets a prayer.
The Outer Gardens. First Terrace of Heaven. Hedges trimmed by angels, pools that reflect nothing unholy. Let us see how they reflect you.
The Gilded Tree bears no fruit any more. Heaven has not noticed. Heaven notices less and less.
The choirs here are slow to anger. Teach them.
Even the gardeners are gone. Somebody left the shears in the hedge, mid-cut, an age ago.
Saint Aurel, Jewel of the Faithful. A mortal city, walled and pious. Every church door is about to open at once.
The bells of Saint Aurel ring the alarm. The faithful bar their doors. Their doors are made of wood.
Narrow streets, narrow minds. Mind the choke points, {demon}. Theirs, not yours.
Listen. The cathedral is singing. Ten thousand mortal voices, and not one answer coming down.
The Frozen Monastery. The Silent Brothers have kept vigil here so long that the cold has learned to pray.
Snow on the meditation stones. Bring the fire indoors, {demon}. All of it.
The wind cuts. The monks cut harder. You cut hardest.
Skarn knows this kind of silence. It is the silence of a cell after the screaming stops.
The Sunlit Citadel, Bastion of the Unsetting Sun. Heaven's war-fortress. Behind its golden rings, the road climbs toward the Seventh Gate.
The Citadel still burns from the last time. Heaven's remnant wants it back. Let them try.
Lancers on the ramparts, archons in the gates. Every courtyard is a siege. You are the siege.
The Citadel's lancers have heard about the March. They are holding the walls with their eyes shut.
The Gilded Isles. A shard of paradise adrift above an endless sea of cloud. Do not look down. Heaven never does.
One bridge joins the halves of the isle. Hold it, and Heaven has to come to you.
Marble, gold, stained glass, and under all of it, nothing for a thousand miles. Fall, {demon}, and keep falling, all the way home.
The sky rift hums the same note over and over. A question. Nobody upstairs is answering it.
The Storm Spire. Heaven's lightning is born here, wound tight around a tower of white stone. Every bolt is a prayer that missed.
Thunder rolls up the Spire like a choir clearing its throat. Make it choke.
Rain falls upward here. Even the weather is trying to leave.
A tower. Good. I have not broken a tower in a while.
Heaven's Gate. The pearl road, the warded arches, and at the end of it, the Seventh Gate, which has never been opened from the outside.
The Seventh Gate does not know your name yet. Break its wards anyway. It is good practice.
Kesh's halberd rings behind you and the Breach opens wider than it ever has. This is the March, {demon}. Break the wards. Fell the warden. Walk through.
The wards of the Seventh Gate glow on their pillars. Break them, fell the warden, and the stairs are yours.
The Gate you broke has been rebuilt by loyalists who will not accept an answer. Break it again.
The Breach. Here Hell came up through the floor of Heaven like a fist through a stained-glass window. Hellfire in the rifts, obsidian through the marble. Ours, nearly.
Every rift here glows with the Pit's own fire. Heaven bleeds light; the wound bleeds back.
The blight has already taken half the island. Take the other half, {demon}.
Home has a door into Heaven now. I should knock.
Kesh says the Breach is wider every week. Standing in it, you understand why: Heaven is not holding it shut. It is falling in.
The defenders here sing as they die. Listen for the reply. There is still none.
Heaven fights hardest here, for every scorched step. As if there were still someone upstairs to disappoint.
The March passes through the Breach. Every demon in the Pit is behind you, {demon}, pressing upward.
The Breach is Hell's front porch now. The loyalists keep trying to sweep it.
A hole in Heaven. The finest cell door I have ever seen. Open.
Flowers. Fruit. Nectar. Children, we are home.
The cold bites the hive. Nhazgul draws the swarm in close, a coat of a million wings. The monks will warm them up.
The pearl road. I walked it every morning for a thousand years. It has not changed. I have.
Iscariel walks the hedges he once patrolled. A gardener-cherub recognises him, drops its shears, and flees.
